advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the SHA-pin gate to recurse into local composite actions referenced by `./`-prefixed uses so their internal third-party `uses:` are also SHA-pinned
evidence: tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py: `if u.startswith("./"):` `continue`
release.yml now uses `./.github/actions/setup-uv`, which internally uses `actions/cache@v6`
The gate only inspects `_text()` of release.yml, not the referenced composite action's steps
advisory.finding: The release SHA-pin gate (test_release_workflow_pins.py) skips `./`-prefixed local actions but does not recurse into the local composite action, so the transitive `actions/cache@v6` used inside .github/actions/setup-uv is never checked for SHA pinning even though release.yml depends on it.
scenarios: A future edit to the composite action adds another unpinned third-party action; the release pin gate passes because it only scans release.yml top-level uses

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tie the committed uv SHA256 checksums to the exact [tool.uv] required-version so a version bump forces a checksum update (single source of truth), or have the guard assert the two checksum copies match against the pinned version
evidence: scripts/check_uv_pin.py hardcodes REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS with fixed digests and compares `actual != expected` against them
The action reads `$version` dynamically from pyproject.toml but the env checksums are static: `.github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml` UV_SHA256_* env vars carry no version tag
The guard `check_local_action` never reads the pyproject version when validating checksums — no coupling between required-version and REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS
advisory.finding: The committed uv artifact SHA256 checksums in the action and in check_uv_pin.py's REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS are not tied to the uv version in pyproject.toml's [tool.uv] required-version, so a version bump without a synchronized checksum update is not caught by the guard (it silently trusts hardcoded digests for a possibly-different version).
scenarios: Someone bumps [tool.uv] required-version to a new uv release and updates the action's env checksums, but forgets to update REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS in check_uv_pin.py (or vice versa), leaving two hardcoded checksum sets that can silently diverge

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/local-dev-env.md (lines 78, 85-89) to describe the repository-local ./.github/actions/setup-uv action that downloads the pinned release artifact with committed checksums, and remove the claim that the manifest fetch / bug 5caa-4b63-7ea2-4e71 is still outstanding.
evidence: docs/local-dev-env.md:78 `The pin also makes CI's uv deterministic. \`astral-sh/setup-uv\` is SHA-pinned at all 25 call` — no workflow uses astral-sh/setup-uv after this change; every site in the diff swaps to `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-uv`.

docs/local-dev-env.md:85-89 `It does **not** yet remove the network dependency itself: the action fetches that same manifest a second time... the \`##[error]fetch failed\` failure mode (bug \`56b7-b21a-c8ab-4afc\`...) is still reachable — tracked as bug \`5caa-4b63-7ea2-4e71\`.` — this change removes that manifest fetch and is the resolution of 5caa.

scripts/check_uv_pin.py:4-18 (changed) now states the local action 'downloads the version-pinned release artifact directly' and adds guard case 5 'Bypassed through the upstream action', confirming the mechanism described in local-dev-env.md is superseded.

docs/README.md:72 `- **[local-dev-env.md](local-dev-env.md)**. Checkout-specific environment setup for development commands and gates.` establishes local-dev-env.md as a maintained internal-documentation surface owning CI/uv setup guidance.
Ticket 5caa-4b63-7ea2-4e71 plan-review manifest lists `read-path: docs/local-dev-env.md` as a currency basis, confirming this page is the owner responsible for describing the changed behavior.
advisory.finding: docs/local-dev-env.md still describes the pre-change CI uv-install mechanism as current: it states astral-sh/setup-uv is SHA-pinned at all 25 call sites, that the action fetches the manifest a second time so the `##[error]fetch failed` mode is still reachable, and that this residual is tracked as unresolved bug 5caa-4b63-7ea2-4e71. This change replaces every call site with ./.github/actions/setup-uv and removes the manifest fetch (it IS ticket 5caa), so the maintained page's current-state description is now inaccurate.
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/local-dev-env.md, correct the current-state prose: replace the 'astral-sh/setup-uv is SHA-pinned at all 25 call sites' statement with a description of the repository-local ./.github/actions/setup-uv composite action, and rewrite lines 85-89 so they no longer describe the second manifest fetch as reachable or bug 5caa-4b63-7ea2-4e71 as an open residual, since this change removes the manifest fetch and resolves that bug.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the action emit the documented anchor 'Successfully installed uv version <pin>' (or update AC-1/CHANGELOG greps to the new phrasing) so the liveness anchor and the verification grep agree.
evidence: action.yml:98: `Write-Host "Successfully installed uv $version from $asset"`
CHANGELOG.md:218: `Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7` with no `Could not determine uv version` fallback.
pyproject.toml:340: `# \`Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7\` across every job of the matrix`
Ticket 5caa AC-1: 'the liveness anchor `Successfully installed uv version <pinned>` ... The anchor is asserted FIRST — a zero-match grep alone is also produced by an empty log or a skipped step'
The guard test only asserts the substring 'Successfully installed uv $version' (test_uv_pin_guard.py:247), so it does not catch that the anchor phrasing diverged from the AC-documented one.
action.yml:96: `& $installedUv --version`
action.yml:98: `Write-Host "Successfully installed uv $version from $asset"` runs regardless of the probe's exit code

PowerShell native-command exit codes only become terminating when $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference is $true (7.4+ default) — on other pwsh versions $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' does not catch a nonzero native exit.
dropped.finding: The local action's install-liveness line is 'Successfully installed uv $version from $asset' (rendering 'Successfully installed uv 0.12.7 from ...'), but the ticket's AC-1 anchor and the repo's established anchor are 'Successfully installed uv version <pinned>' (the word 'version' is dropped). A grep for the documented anchor will silently produce zero matches against the new logs — the exact vacuous-pass failure mode AC-1 was written to prevent.
merged_from: The post-install health probe `& $installedUv --version` never reads the process exit status, and the terminal 'Successfully installed' message is printed unconditionally afterward. Under Windows PowerShell / PowerShell without $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference, a nonzero exit from the version probe does not raise, so a corrupt-but-checksum-matching or ABI-incompatible binary reports success.
dropped.suggested_fix: Change the Write-Host to `Write-Host "Successfully installed uv version $version from $asset"` (and update the guard-test substring to match), so the AC-1 grep for 'Successfully installed uv version <pin>' matches.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Align `_is_exact_specifier` with the action's regex (require at least one dot / full X.Y.Z form) so the gate and the installer agree on what is a valid pin.
evidence: check_uv_pin.py:89-93: accepts remainder when `remainder[0].isdigit()` and `all(part.isdigit() ...)` — '5' passes
action.yml:32: `'^required-version\s*=\s*"==([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)+)"'` requires `(?:\.[0-9]+)+`, i.e. at least one dot
dropped.finding: The Python exact-specifier acceptor and the action's PowerShell version regex classify differently: `_is_exact_specifier` accepts a single-segment release like '==5' (remainder '5' is all-digits), but the action's regex '^required-version\s*=\s*"==([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)+)"' requires at least one dot and would fail to parse it. A pin the gate passes could therefore be un-installable by the action.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin `actions/cache@v6` to a full 40-char commit SHA in .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml
evidence: .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml: `uses: actions/cache@v6`

Contrast with SHA-pinned peers in workflows: `actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0` and the removed `astral-sh/setup-uv@ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d  # v10.0.0`
The test fixture in tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py also uses `uses: actions/cache@v6`
dropped.finding: The local composite action pins third-party actions with a mutable major-version tag `actions/cache@v6` instead of a full commit SHA, reintroducing an unpinned third-party action into the supply chain that the repo otherwise SHA-pins everywhere.
scenarios: actions/cache v6 tag is force-pushed or compromised, silently altering cache save/restore behavior across all CI jobs that now route through the local action
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace `uses: actions/cache@v6` with the corresponding full commit SHA and a `# v6.x.y` comment, matching the SHA-pin convention used for setup-python and the former setup-uv reference.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or add) how the committed uv SHA256 digests are sourced/verified against astral-sh's signed release checksums, and consider attestation verification
evidence: .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml: `Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $archive` then `Get-FileHash ... -Algorithm SHA256` compared to committed env value
No verification of upstream astral-sh signing/attestation is performed
dropped.finding: The downloaded uv release artifact is verified only by a committed SHA256 hash, with no signature or provenance attestation (e.g. cosign/SLSA) check, so the trust root is entirely the manually-committed digest and the integrity of GitHub's release download endpoint.
scenarios: The committed checksum itself was captured from a compromised or non-canonical source when first added, since there is no cross-check against astral-sh's signed release manifest

evidence: .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml:73-75 'if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "Checksum mismatch ..." }' — the core artifact-integrity contract
scripts/check_uv_pin.py:287-298 only compares env checksum strings to REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS, not the install script's verification behavior

dropped.finding: The action's PowerShell install logic — the substantive new behavior — has no behavioral coverage for its security-critical checksum-mismatch rejection path. The gate only asserts the committed checksum env values equal a hardcoded Python copy; it never exercises download/verify/extract, so a broken 'Checksum mismatch ... throw' would not be caught.
